messages:
alex_w: Heads-up — ran into a confusing cred precedence bug in the Python quickstart sample.

maria_g: ugh, details?

alex_w: Quick repro: sample README tells users to set REDWOOD_API_KEY, but the snippet in quickstart.py reads REDWOOD_KEY (typo). So new users sometimes end up with no env key and fall back to the global in-memory placeholder.

chris_t: oh no. Is that just a docs mismatch or does the SDK make it worse?

alex_w: Both. Docs typo triggers different fallback, but the SDK also has this surprising precedence: constructor arg > env var > global client.default_key. However in async paths when creating multiple clients at once we hit a race where the global default_key gets clobbered. Repro below.

samir_r: can you paste the minimal repro?

alex_w: sure:

```py
# repro_async_leak.py
import asyncio
from redwood import RedwoodClient

async def make_and_call(key, n=1):
    client = RedwoodClient(api_key=key)
    for _ in range(n):
        await client.generate("hello")

async def main():
    tasks = [make_and_call(f"key-{i}", 3) for i in range(4)]
    await asyncio.gather(*tasks)

asyncio.run(main())
```

alex_w: Expected: each client uses its own key. Observed: some requests show auth failures and some succeed with another client's key. Logs show rapid flips of client._effective_key pointing to the wrong string.

maria_g: that looks bad. Any stack traces?

alex_w: snippet from logs: 
```
2026-03-18T15:01:12.123Z client[key-2] -> POST /v1/generate 200
2026-03-18T15:01:12.124Z client[key-1] -> POST /v1/generate 401 (invalid_api_key)
2026-03-18T15:01:12.124Z client[key-3] -> POST /v1/generate 401 (invalid_api_key)
```

alex_w: Investigated: implementation uses a mutable global credentials registry plus a fast-path that consults a module-level cache. When async tasks interleave, the cache returns the wrong entry.

chris_t: is this the same cache used for token refreshes?

alex_w: Related code paths yes — refresh and precedence resolution share the cache. Also typing/DX issue: CredentialProvider is an internal type with no public typing or easy subclassing, so external users can't plug in a deterministic provider easily.

samir_r: What are immediate mitigations?

alex_w: Workarounds we tried: 1) pass api_key explicitly to every client (good but painful for sample apps), 2) set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var correctly (good for single-tenant runs), 3) set a unique client_name and avoid global registry (hacky).

maria_g: Proposed fix?

alex_w: Short-term: hotfix to make credential resolution instance-bound (no module-level mutation) and add an integration test that spawns many async clients concurrently. Also patch quickstart to use REDWOOD_API_KEY consistently and show the explicit constructor param recommended for multi-client apps.

chris_t: long-term: expose a stable CredentialProvider protocol (typing.Protocol) that users can implement or pass into RedwoodClient(..., credential_provider=...). Docs should include precedence table and a recommended pattern for async multi-client usage.

samir_r: agreed. Also add lint rule or CI check to catch env var name mismatches between README and code samples.

alex_w: one more DX note: the async client lacks a clear context manager example. Users think creating clients cheaply is fine; we should document "create once and reuse" and provide an async contextmanager snippet.

maria_g: can someone open a PR for the quickstart docs + small SDK change?

chris_t: I'll open the SDK PR with the instance-bound fix + test. tagging @maria_g for quickstart doc PR. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Note: issue created in repo redwood/redwood-py #482: "py: fix credential cache race & improve credential provider typing"

alex_w: thanks all — will validate once PR lands.

maria_g: thanks for catching this — saves onboarding headaches. :raised_hands:
